notes:
Small SMB in field-service scheduling. Inbound, self-serve lead now in discovery. Primary goal: low-latency streaming to their agent UI plus reliable tool-calling to trigger backend actions such as create_job and estimate_arrival. Current issue summary: when they enable structured JSON output together with streaming and provided function definitions, responses intermittently cause client-side parse failures or result in tool invocations with missing parameters. They report about 1 in 6 runs failing; causes appear to be a mix of chunked streaming boundaries breaking their parser and type mismatches between declared function parameter schemas and values returned by the runtime.

What they attempted: provided function schemas and set response.stream=true; built a client incremental parser but it fails when chunks split JSON tokens; server logs sometimes show tool invocation with empty parameter payloads or numeric IDs sent as strings.

Quotes: "It works most of the time but random parse failures break the agent UI — can't ship like that."

SE observations: repro is intermittent, likely client parser expects full-token chunks. Also saw schema mismatches (ints vs strings). Short-term mitigation discussed: 1) add tolerant client-side streaming JSON assembler that buffers until valid object boundaries, 2) temporarily turn off strict structured mode and post-process text on server, 3) loosen function parameter requirements (make fields optional or accept string/int) where safe. SE to provide a minimal resilient streaming parser snippet for browser/node and checklist of request headers that affect streaming.

Risks: customer is time-sensitive and cost-conscious; poor UX could cause quick churn.

Next steps: schedule 30m triage with SE (Kai) + owner + dev; SE to drop code sample in Drive; validate schemas against runtime and escalate if runtime mutates params during streaming. Stubs: Fireflies ff_20260301_01, Drive repro link, Support INF-2378.
